assemblies.name: Interior partition demolition
assemblies.why: Wall area is drawn length times height; debris is the wall's solid volume times 1.4 for the air between broken pieces, rounded up to 20 CY roll-off containers.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Floor finish removal
assemblies.why: Removal is the floor area. Scraping adhesive is counted on the same area; debris uses a quarter inch of material plus bulking, which is small, so one container usually covers a floor.

assemblies.name: Ceiling removal
assemblies.why: Ceiling area plus grid and tile debris at about one cubic yard per 250 SF, a common rule for lay-in ceilings.

assemblies.name: Concrete slab removal
assemblies.why: Slab volume is area times thickness. Concrete in place weighs about 2 tons a cubic yard (150 lb a CF) and swells about 40 percent when broken and loaded, so the haul volume is larger but the weight is not.

assemblies.name: Fixture and device removal
assemblies.why: One removal per counted item, with a cap or plate to make each disconnected point safe.

assemblies.name: Slab on grade, 4 in
assemblies.why: Concrete is area times 4 in over 27 to get cubic yards, with 5 percent waste for subgrade variation and spillage. Vapor retarder laps add 10 percent. Wire mesh comes in 8 x 20 ft sheets (160 SF) with 10 percent lap waste. Curing compound covers about 200 SF a gallon.

assemblies.name: Slab on grade, 5 in
assemblies.why: Concrete is area times 5 in over 27 to get cubic yards, with 5 percent waste for subgrade variation and spillage. Vapor retarder laps add 10 percent. Wire mesh comes in 8 x 20 ft sheets (160 SF) with 10 percent lap waste. Curing compound covers about 200 SF a gallon.

assemblies.name: Slab on grade, 6 in
assemblies.why: Concrete is area times 6 in over 27 to get cubic yards, with 5 percent waste for subgrade variation and spillage. Vapor retarder laps add 10 percent. Rebar runs both ways at the spacing given; 0.668 lb per foot is the weight of a #4 bar; chairs at one per 16 SF. Curing compound covers about 200 SF a gallon.

assemblies.name: Concrete by measured volume
assemblies.why: For any volume measured with a depth: cubic yards with 5 percent waste, plus a pump or truck charge counted once per pour (one per measurement).

assemblies.name: Continuous wall footing
assemblies.why: Concrete is length times width times depth. Longitudinal bars run the full length with 10 percent for laps and waste; side forms are both faces of the footing depth.

assemblies.name: Spread footing
assemblies.why: Each counted footing is length times width times depth. Bars run both ways at the spacing: the bars along the length are spread across the width and the bars along the width across the length, each bar the footing dimension less 3 in cover at each end.

assemblies.name: Foundation wall, cast in place
assemblies.why: Concrete is length times height times thickness. Forms cover both faces. Vertical bars at the spacing over the height, horizontal bars at the spacing over the length, plus 10 percent for laps. Each form tie passes through the wall and holds both faces, one tie per 4 SF of wall (2 x 2 ft spacing).

assemblies.name: Grade beam
assemblies.why: Concrete is the beam section times length; four continuous bars and stirrups at the spacing, each stirrup the section perimeter.

assemblies.name: Drilled pier
assemblies.why: Each pier is a cylinder: 3.1416 times radius squared times depth, with 10 percent overbreak because drilled holes run larger than the auger.

assemblies.name: Concrete column
assemblies.why: Each column is width times depth times height; forms are the four faces; ties at the spacing over the height.

assemblies.name: Elevated slab
assemblies.why: Concrete is area times thickness; deck forms or shoring cover the full area; two mats of bars at the spacing.

assemblies.name: Concrete topping
assemblies.why: A thin topping is area times thickness; bonding compound covers about 300 SF a gallon.

assemblies.name: Concrete sealer
assemblies.why: Penetrating sealer covers about 250 SF a gallon a coat; two coats are typical.

assemblies.name: Expansion joint
assemblies.why: Joint filler strips run the drawn length in 10 ft pieces, with sealant over the top.

assemblies.name: Concrete stair
assemblies.why: Count each flight. Volume is the waist slab plus the risers' triangles: with 7 in risers, 11 in treads and a 6 in waist that is about 0.13 CY per riser for a 4 ft wide stair.

assemblies.name: Concrete block wall, 6 in
assemblies.why: A standard 8 x 16 in face block covers 0.889 SF, so walls take 1.125 blocks a SF. Mortar runs about 3 bags per 100 blocks. Grouting every cell of a 6 in wall takes about 0.17 CF a SF of wall; ladder joint reinforcement goes in every other course (every 16 in).

assemblies.name: Concrete block wall, 8 in
assemblies.why: A standard 8 x 16 in face block covers 0.889 SF, so walls take 1.125 blocks a SF. Mortar runs about 3 bags per 100 blocks. Grouting every cell of a 8 in wall takes about 0.26 CF a SF of wall; ladder joint reinforcement goes in every other course (every 16 in).

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Concrete block wall, 12 in
assemblies.why: A standard 8 x 16 in face block covers 0.889 SF, so walls take 1.125 blocks a SF. Mortar runs about 3 bags per 100 blocks. Grouting every cell of a 12 in wall takes about 0.43 CF a SF of wall; ladder joint reinforcement goes in every other course (every 16 in).

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Brick veneer
assemblies.why: Modular brick with 3/8 in joints is 6.86 brick a SF. Mortar is about 7 CF per 1,000 brick. Wall ties go one per 2.67 SF (16 in by 24 in); flashing and weeps at the base run the wall length.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Stone veneer, adhered
assemblies.why: Adhered stone is sold by face area; corners are counted separately in practice, so 10 percent waste covers cutting. Scratch coat and mortar at about one 80 lb bag per 20 SF.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Block by wall area
assemblies.why: For a wall elevation measured as an area: 1.125 standard blocks a SF and 3 bags of mortar per 100 blocks.

assemblies.name: Masonry cleaning
assemblies.why: Masonry cleaner covers about 100 SF a gallon at working strength.

assemblies.name: Pipe handrail
assemblies.why: Rail runs the drawn length; posts at the spacing plus one at the end of each run; brackets every 4 ft on walls.

assemblies.name: Guardrail
assemblies.why: Top and mid rails run the length, posts at the spacing plus one per run, pickets at 4 in clear.

assemblies.name: Steel lintel
assemblies.why: Each counted opening gets an angle the opening width plus 8 in bearing at each end.

assemblies.name: Steel floor deck
assemblies.why: Deck sheets cover their width; 5 percent for end laps and cuts. Puddle welds at about one per 4 SF.

assemblies.name: Cold-formed steel studs, load bearing
assemblies.why: Studs at the spacing over the length plus one per wall end; top and bottom track run the length twice.

assemblies.name: Pipe bollard
assemblies.why: Each bollard is a pipe the exposed height plus embedment, filled with concrete.

assemblies.name: Steel stair
assemblies.why: Count each flight: treads and risers per flight, two stringers the flight's run.

assemblies.name: Wood stud wall, 2x4 at 16 in
assemblies.why: Studs at 16 in centers over the length, plus one per wall end and two for each corner or opening (the openings parameter). Plates are one bottom and two top, so three times the length, in 16 ft stock.

params.name: Corners and openings to add studs for

assemblies.name: Wood stud wall, 2x4 at 24 in
assemblies.why: Studs at 24 in centers over the length, plus one per wall end and two for each corner or opening (the openings parameter). Plates are one bottom and two top, so three times the length, in 16 ft stock.

params.name: Corners and openings to add studs for

assemblies.name: Wood stud wall, 2x6 at 16 in
assemblies.why: Studs at 16 in centers over the length, plus one per wall end and two for each corner or opening (the openings parameter). Plates are one bottom and two top, so three times the length, in 16 ft stock.

params.name: Corners and openings to add studs for

assemblies.name: Wood stud wall, 2x6 at 24 in
assemblies.why: Studs at 24 in centers over the length, plus one per wall end and two for each corner or opening (the openings parameter). Plates are one bottom and two top, so three times the length, in 16 ft stock.

params.name: Corners and openings to add studs for

assemblies.name: Floor joists, 2x10 at 16 in
assemblies.why: Joist length per square foot is 12 / 16 at 16 in centers. Rim board runs the perimeter of the area; blocking or bridging at mid span adds about 10 percent.

assemblies.name: Floor joists, 2x12 at 16 in
assemblies.why: Joist length per square foot is 12 / 16 at 16 in centers. Rim board runs the perimeter of the area; blocking or bridging at mid span adds about 10 percent.

assemblies.name: Floor joists, I-joist at 19.2 in
assemblies.why: Joist length per square foot is 12 / 19.2 at 19.2 in centers. Rim board runs the perimeter of the area; blocking or bridging at mid span adds about 10 percent.

assemblies.name: Subfloor, 3/4 in panels
assemblies.why: Panels are 4 x 8 ft (32 SF) with 10 percent for cutting; one tube of subfloor adhesive does about 3 panels.

assemblies.name: Wall sheathing
assemblies.why: Wall area over 32 SF per 4 x 8 panel with 10 percent for openings cut out and waste.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Roof sheathing
assemblies.why: Roof area (with pitch) over 32 SF per panel, 10 percent waste for hips and valleys, and one panel clip per panel edge between rafters.

assemblies.name: Roof trusses
assemblies.why: Draw the ridge or the wall the trusses bear on: trusses at the spacing over the length, plus one, and the gable ends.

assemblies.name: Rafters
assemblies.why: Rafter length per square foot of roof is 12 over the spacing; ridge and ceiling joists are counted separately.

assemblies.name: Blocking
assemblies.why: Solid blocking along the drawn line in 8 ft stock with 15 percent for short pieces.

assemblies.name: Baseboard, wood
assemblies.why: Trim runs the drawn length; 10 percent covers miters and short ends, bought in 16 ft pieces.

assemblies.name: Crown molding
assemblies.why: Crown takes more waste than base (15 percent) for compound miters, in 16 ft pieces.

assemblies.name: Door casing
assemblies.why: Each door gets casing on both sides: two legs and a head per side, about 17 LF a side for a 3 x 7 door.

assemblies.name: Window casing and stool
assemblies.why: Each window gets its perimeter in casing plus a stool and apron the width.

assemblies.name: Base cabinets
assemblies.why: Base cabinets by running length; fillers and end panels add about 5 percent.

assemblies.name: Wall cabinets
assemblies.why: Wall cabinets by running length; fillers add about 5 percent.

assemblies.name: Countertop
assemblies.why: Countertop area is the run times the depth (25.5 in standard) with 10 percent for seams and overhangs; backsplash runs the same length.

assemblies.name: Shelving
assemblies.why: Shelf length times the number of shelves, with standards every 32 in.

assemblies.name: Wood deck
assemblies.why: Deck boards cover their width plus the gap: LF of board per SF is 12 over (width plus gap). Joists at 16 in.

assemblies.name: Fascia board
assemblies.why: Fascia runs the eave and rake length in 16 ft stock with 10 percent for joints.

assemblies.name: Soffit
assemblies.why: Soffit panels cover the soffit area with 10 percent for cutting; vents every 10 ft are counted separately.

assemblies.name: Wood stair
assemblies.why: Count each flight: treads and risers per flight and three stringers.

assemblies.name: Batt insulation, R-13, 2x4 walls
assemblies.why: Batts cover the framed area; 5 percent for cutting around boxes and blocking. Bags hold the square feet given (it varies by product, so set it from the label).

assemblies.name: Batt insulation, R-21, 2x6 walls
assemblies.why: Batts cover the framed area; 5 percent for cutting around boxes and blocking. Bags hold the square feet given (it varies by product, so set it from the label).

assemblies.name: Batt insulation, R-30, ceilings
assemblies.why: Batts cover the framed area; 5 percent for cutting around boxes and blocking. Bags hold the square feet given (it varies by product, so set it from the label).

assemblies.name: Batt insulation, R-38, ceilings
assemblies.why: Batts cover the framed area; 5 percent for cutting around boxes and blocking. Bags hold the square feet given (it varies by product, so set it from the label).

assemblies.name: Blown attic insulation
assemblies.why: Loose fill: bags per SF at the target depth come from the bag chart; the default is about 40 SF a bag at R-38.

params.name: Square feet per bag at the target R

assemblies.name: Rigid board insulation
assemblies.why: 4 x 8 boards (32 SF) with 5 percent waste; fasteners or adhesive at about 8 per board.

assemblies.name: Spray foam insulation
assemblies.why: Spray foam is sold by board foot: area times thickness in inches; 10 percent for overspray and trimming.

assemblies.name: Weather barrier wrap
assemblies.why: Wrap covers the wall area with 10 percent for laps; a 9 x 150 ft roll covers 1,350 SF; tape runs the seams.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Vapor retarder
assemblies.why: Sheet covers the area with 10 percent for 6 in laps; rolls of 10 x 100 ft (1,000 SF).

assemblies.name: Asphalt shingle roof
assemblies.why: Draw the roof with its pitch so the area is the true slope area. A square is 100 SF, three bundles a square, 10 percent waste for hips and valleys (15 percent on cut-up roofs). Drip edge runs the area's perimeter.

assemblies.name: Metal roof panels
assemblies.why: Panels cover the sloped area with 5 percent for end laps and trim cuts; fasteners about 80 per square.

assemblies.name: Single-ply membrane roof
assemblies.why: Membrane rolls of 10 x 100 ft with 10 percent for seams and flashing; insulation boards 4 x 8 with plates and screws at about 8 per board.

assemblies.name: Modified bitumen roof
assemblies.why: Rolls cover about one square each after laps, two plies, 10 percent waste.

assemblies.name: Built-up roof, 4 ply
assemblies.why: Four plies of felt (each roll about 4 squares) and asphalt at about 25 lb per square per ply.

assemblies.name: Roof underlayment
assemblies.why: Synthetic underlayment rolls cover about 1,000 SF with laps; 10 percent waste.

assemblies.name: Gutters and downspouts
assemblies.why: Gutter runs the drawn eave length; hangers every 2 ft; one downspout per 35 ft of gutter (and at least one per run).

assemblies.name: Sheet metal flashing
assemblies.why: Flashing runs the drawn length in 10 ft pieces with 4 in laps (about 5 percent).

assemblies.name: Joint sealant
assemblies.why: A 10.1 oz tube fills about 24 LF of a 1/4 x 1/4 in joint; the default joint size gives the LF per tube.

assemblies.name: Firestopping at penetrations
assemblies.why: One firestop system per counted penetration; a tube of sealant does about four small pipe penetrations.

assemblies.name: Below-grade waterproofing
assemblies.why: Sheet membrane covers the wall area below grade with 10 percent for laps; protection board over it.

assemblies.name: Dampproofing
assemblies.why: Asphalt dampproofing covers about 50 SF a gallon a coat on concrete.

assemblies.name: Vinyl siding
assemblies.why: Siding is sold by the square (100 SF) with 10 percent waste; J channel around openings and corner posts are counted from the openings and corners parameters.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Fiber cement lap siding
assemblies.why: Planks cover their exposure: plank LF per SF is 12 over the exposure in inches, in 12 ft planks, 10 percent waste.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Portland cement stucco
assemblies.why: Three coats total about 7/8 in; one bag of cement plaster covers about 12 SF at that thickness; lath under it.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Exterior insulation and finish system
assemblies.why: Foam board 2 x 4 ft (8 SF), mesh and base coat over the area, finish coat at about 100 SF a pail.

assemblies.name: Interior door, prehung
assemblies.why: Each counted door: the slab and frame, three hinges, a lockset and a door stop.

assemblies.name: Exterior door
assemblies.why: Each counted door: prehung unit, threshold, weatherstripping set, deadbolt and lockset.

assemblies.name: Hollow metal door and frame
assemblies.why: Each counted opening: frame, door, and anchors (about three per jamb).

assemblies.name: Door hardware set
assemblies.why: A typical set per counted door: hinges (3), lever set, closer and wall stop.

assemblies.name: Windows
assemblies.why: Each counted window: the unit, flashing tape around its perimeter with 10 percent lap, and sealant.

assemblies.name: Aluminum storefront
assemblies.why: Storefront by elevation: length times height in glass area, mullions every 5 ft.

assemblies.name: Overhead sectional door
assemblies.why: Each counted door: the door with its track, and an operator. Doors are ordered to the opening size, so there is no waste.

assemblies.name: Skylight
assemblies.why: Each counted skylight with the curb flashing kit made for it; a skylight is a unit, so there is no waste factor.

assemblies.name: Access panel
assemblies.why: One panel per counted opening; panels are made to size, so the count is the order.

assemblies.name: Gypsum board wall, 1/2 in, one side
assemblies.why: Board area is wall area times 1 side(s) times 1 layer(s) over 32 SF a 4 x 8 sheet, with 10 percent waste for openings and offcuts. Screws run about one per SF of board, in boxes of 1,000; joint compound about 1 gallon per 100 SF of taped face (4.5 gallon pails) and tape about 0.37 LF per SF.

Screws run about one per SF of board, in boxes of 1,000; joint compound about 1 gallon per 100 SF of taped face (4.5 gallon pails) and tape about 0.37 LF per SF.

assemblies.name: Gypsum board wall, 5/8 in Type X, both sides
assemblies.why: Board area is wall area times 2 side(s) times 1 layer(s) over 32 SF a 4 x 8 sheet, with 10 percent waste for openings and offcuts. Screws run about one per SF of board, in boxes of 1,000; joint compound about 1 gallon per 100 SF of taped face (4.5 gallon pails) and tape about 0.37 LF per SF.

assemblies.name: Gypsum board wall, 5/8 in Type X, two layers each side
assemblies.why: Board area is wall area times 2 side(s) times 2 layer(s) over 32 SF a 4 x 8 sheet, with 10 percent waste for openings and offcuts. Screws run about one per SF of board, in boxes of 1,000; joint compound about 1 gallon per 100 SF of taped face (4.5 gallon pails) and tape about 0.37 LF per SF.

assemblies.name: Gypsum board ceiling
assemblies.why: Ceiling board, 1/2 in sag-resistant, over 32 SF a sheet with 10 percent waste; compound and tape as on walls.

assemblies.name: Moisture-resistant board
assemblies.why: Wet-area walls, one side, over 32 SF a sheet with 10 percent waste.

assemblies.name: Cement backer board
assemblies.why: Backer board 3 x 5 ft (15 SF) with 10 percent waste; screws at about 1 per SF and mesh tape on seams.

assemblies.name: Metal stud partition with board both sides
assemblies.why: Studs at the spacing plus one per wall end, top and bottom track, and 5/8 in board both sides over 32 SF a sheet.

assemblies.name: Acoustical ceiling, 2 x 2 ft
assemblies.why: Tiles at 4 SF each with 5 percent for border cuts. Main runners every 4 ft (SF / 4 LF), cross tees fill the module (one 4 ft or 2 ft tee per tile on 2 x 2, one 4 ft tee per tile on 2 x 4), wall angle runs the room perimeter, and a hanger wire every 16 SF.

assemblies.name: Acoustical ceiling, 2 x 4 ft
assemblies.why: Tiles at 8 SF each with 5 percent for border cuts. Main runners every 4 ft (SF / 4 LF), cross tees fill the module (one 4 ft or 2 ft tee per tile on 2 x 2, one 4 ft tee per tile on 2 x 4), wall angle runs the room perimeter, and a hanger wire every 16 SF.

assemblies.name: Paint walls, primer and two coats
assemblies.why: Paint covers about 350 SF a gallon a coat on smooth board; primer the same. 5 percent for touch-up and loss.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Paint ceilings
assemblies.why: Flat ceiling paint covers about 350 SF a gallon a coat on primed board; 5 percent covers loss in the tray and touch-up.

assemblies.name: Paint trim
assemblies.why: Trim paints about 1 SF per LF of 4 in trim; a quart covers about 100 SF.

assemblies.name: Paint doors and frames
assemblies.why: A door and frame both sides is about 50 SF; at 350 SF a gallon a coat.

assemblies.name: Stain and clear finish
assemblies.why: Stain covers about 250 SF a gallon; clear coat about 400 SF a gallon a coat.

assemblies.name: Epoxy floor coating
assemblies.why: Two-part epoxy kits cover about 250 SF a coat; primer one coat and two finish coats.

assemblies.name: Broadloom carpet
assemblies.why: Carpet is sold by the square yard (9 SF) from 12 ft rolls; 10 percent covers seams and pattern match. Pad matches the carpet; tack strip runs the room perimeter.

assemblies.name: Carpet tile
assemblies.why: 24 x 24 in tiles (4 SF) with 5 percent for border cuts; adhesive about 400 SF a gallon.

assemblies.name: Resilient sheet flooring
assemblies.why: Sheet goods from 6 or 12 ft rolls; 10 percent for seams and fitting.

assemblies.name: Luxury vinyl tile or plank
assemblies.why: Planks come in cartons; the default carton covers 24 SF; 7 percent waste for straight lay.

assemblies.name: Vinyl composition tile
assemblies.why: 12 x 12 in tile, 45 to a box, 5 percent waste; adhesive about 200 SF a gallon.

assemblies.name: Ceramic floor tile
assemblies.why: Tile area with 10 percent for cuts (15 percent on a diagonal). Thinset about 50 SF a 50 lb bag with a 1/4 in notch; grout about 1 lb per 8 SF for 12 in tile with 1/8 in joints.

assemblies.name: Ceramic wall tile
assemblies.why: Wall tile over the wall area, 10 percent for cuts; mastic about 50 SF a gallon; grout about 1 lb per 10 SF.

assemblies.name: Large-format porcelain tile
assemblies.why: Large tile with 12 percent waste (less flexible cuts); large-format mortar about 40 SF a bag; leveling clips about 4 per tile.

assemblies.name: Hardwood flooring
assemblies.why: Strip hardwood with 7 percent waste for end cuts (10 percent on diagonals); underlayment paper and cleats at about 1 per SF.

assemblies.name: Laminate flooring
assemblies.why: Floating laminate in cartons (default 20 SF) with 8 percent waste; foam underlayment rolls of 100 SF.

assemblies.name: Resilient base
assemblies.why: Rubber or vinyl base in 120 ft coils with 5 percent waste; adhesive one tube per 40 LF; outside corners are counted separately.

assemblies.name: Self-leveling underlayment
assemblies.why: A 50 lb bag covers about 50 SF at 1/8 in, so bags are area times thickness over 6.25.

assemblies.name: Wallcovering
assemblies.why: A double roll gives about 56 SF of usable covering after pattern match; 15 percent extra for matching.

params.name: Wall height when the measurement has none

assemblies.name: Polished concrete floor
assemblies.why: Grinding and polishing by area with densifier at about 400 SF a gallon.

assemblies.name: Toilet compartments
assemblies.why: Each counted compartment: panels, door and one pilaster, plus one extra pilaster per run.

assemblies.name: Toilet accessories set
assemblies.why: Per counted toilet room: grab bars (2), paper dispenser, mirror, soap dispenser and towel dispenser.

assemblies.name: Fire extinguisher and cabinet
assemblies.why: One extinguisher and one cabinet per counted location; travel distance rules set where they go, the count sets how many.

assemblies.name: Room signs
assemblies.why: One sign per counted door or room; signs are made to order, so the count is the order with no waste.

assemblies.name: Metal lockers
assemblies.why: Count each locker; base and end panels about one per six lockers.

assemblies.name: Corner guards
assemblies.why: One guard per counted outside corner, in the height given (4 ft is common in corridors).

assemblies.name: Wall protection rail
assemblies.why: Crash rail along the drawn length in 12 ft pieces with end caps per run.

assemblies.name: Residential appliances
assemblies.why: One appliance per count with its own connection kit (water line, cord or vent), since each one needs a separate hookup.

assemblies.name: Window blinds
assemblies.why: One blind per counted window; blinds are cut to each opening, so there is no waste factor.

assemblies.name: Window sills, solid surface
assemblies.why: Each counted window gets a sill the opening width plus 1 in of horn at each end; 10 percent covers cutting from stock lengths.

assemblies.name: Sprinkler heads
assemblies.why: Each counted head with a drop (arm-over) of pipe and two fittings.

assemblies.name: Sprinklers by floor area
assemblies.why: A budget count of heads: area over the coverage per head (130 SF is common for light hazard design; the code maximum is larger), rounded up, with branch line at about 12 ft per head.

assemblies.name: Fire department connection
assemblies.why: One fire department connection per counted location, with its check valve set as one unit.

assemblies.name: Plumbing fixture rough-in
assemblies.why: Each counted fixture: supply and waste piping allowances in feet, a trap and stop valves.

assemblies.name: Water closets
assemblies.why: Each counted toilet: fixture, seat, wax ring and closet bolts, and a supply line.

assemblies.name: Lavatories
assemblies.why: Each counted lavatory: fixture, faucet, trap and two supply lines.

assemblies.name: Sinks
assemblies.why: Each counted sink: fixture, faucet, basket strainers, trap and supply lines.

assemblies.name: Water heater
assemblies.why: Each counted heater with an expansion tank, relief discharge piping and a pan.

assemblies.name: Floor drains
assemblies.why: Each counted drain with a trap primer connection and 10 ft of waste pipe.

assemblies.name: Domestic water piping
assemblies.why: Pipe along the drawn route with 10 percent for offsets, one fitting per 10 ft, hangers every 6 ft, in 20 ft sticks.

assemblies.name: Drain, waste and vent piping
assemblies.why: Pipe along the route with 10 percent waste, one fitting per 8 ft, hangers every 4 ft, in 10 ft lengths; cement and primer about one quart pair per 100 joints.

assemblies.name: Fuel gas piping
assemblies.why: Black steel or flexible gas pipe along the route, fittings every 10 ft, hangers every 6 ft.

assemblies.name: Cleanouts
assemblies.why: One cleanout per counted location; codes call for them at changes of direction and at set intervals along a run.

assemblies.name: Supply diffusers
assemblies.why: Each counted diffuser with its flex connection (default 8 ft) and a balancing damper.

assemblies.name: Return grilles
assemblies.why: One return grille per counted opening; grilles are sized to the duct, so the count is the order.

assemblies.name: Rectangular ductwork
assemblies.why: Sheet metal weight is the duct perimeter times the length times the sheet weight per SF (24 gauge galvanized is about 1.156 lb/SF), plus 20 percent for seams, joints and hangers.

assemblies.name: Round flexible duct
assemblies.why: Flex duct comes in 25 ft boxes; 10 percent for slack and connections.

assemblies.name: Exhaust fans
assemblies.why: Each counted fan with a roof or wall cap and about 10 ft of duct to the outside, with 10 percent duct waste.

assemblies.name: Thermostats
assemblies.why: One thermostat per counted zone with about 50 ft of control cable back to the equipment.

assemblies.name: Duct insulation wrap
assemblies.why: Wrap covers the duct perimeter times length with 10 percent for laps; tape at the seams.

assemblies.name: Cooling by floor area (budget)
assemblies.why: A budget check only: a common rule is about one ton of cooling per 400 SF of conditioned area. A load calculation sets the real size.

assemblies.name: Duplex receptacles
assemblies.why: Each counted outlet: device, box, cover plate and a branch cable allowance (default 25 ft) in 250 ft coils.

assemblies.name: Switches
assemblies.why: Each counted switch: device, box, plate and a cable allowance (default 20 ft) with 10 percent for terminations.

assemblies.name: Recessed light fixtures
assemblies.why: Each counted fixture with a whip (default 6 ft) and cable allowance.

assemblies.name: Lay-in troffers, 2 x 4
assemblies.why: Each counted troffer with a flexible whip and two independent tie wires from the structure, as lay-in fixtures need in most ceilings.

assemblies.name: Exit and emergency lights
assemblies.why: One exit sign or emergency light per counted location; units are complete with battery, so the count is the order.

assemblies.name: Panelboards
assemblies.why: Each counted panel with its circuit breakers (default 24 spaces).

assemblies.name: EMT conduit with wire
assemblies.why: Conduit along the route in 10 ft sticks with 10 percent for bends; a coupling per stick, a strap every 8 ft, and wire the conduit length times the conductors plus 10 percent for terminations.

assemblies.name: Nonmetallic cable runs
assemblies.why: Cable along the drawn route plus 15 percent for drops and terminations, in 250 ft coils; staples every 4 ft.

assemblies.name: Data outlets
assemblies.why: Each counted outlet: jacks (default 2), faceplate, box and a cable run (default 150 ft, under the 295 ft channel limit).

assemblies.name: Smoke detectors
assemblies.why: Each counted detector with its base and about 30 ft of cable to the next device, plus 10 percent for terminations.

assemblies.name: Lighting by floor area
assemblies.why: A layout check: fixtures at one per the coverage area (64 SF suits 2 x 4 troffers on an 8 ft grid), rounded up.

assemblies.name: Site light poles
assemblies.why: Each counted pole: pole, fixture head(s) and a concrete base.

assemblies.name: Bulk excavation
assemblies.why: Measure the cut as a volume (area times depth). Soil swells about 25 percent when dug; trucks haul about 12 loose CY.

assemblies.name: Trench excavation and backfill
assemblies.why: Trench volume is length times width times depth. Bedding fills 6 in under the pipe; backfill is the rest, with 15 percent extra because compacted soil takes more than its bank volume.

assemblies.name: Fill and compaction
assemblies.why: Compacted fill needs about 25 percent more loose material than its finished volume.

assemblies.name: Fine grading
assemblies.why: Fine grading is priced by the square yard: the drawn area over 9. No waste, since it is a service on the area itself.

assemblies.name: Aggregate base
assemblies.why: Base volume is area times thickness; crushed stone weighs about 1.4 tons a CY placed, and compaction takes about 15 percent more material.

assemblies.name: Topsoil
assemblies.why: Topsoil volume is area times depth, with 15 percent for settling.

assemblies.name: Silt fence
assemblies.why: Fence along the drawn line with stakes every 6 ft, in 100 ft rolls.

assemblies.name: Inlet protection
assemblies.why: One filter per counted storm inlet, kept in place until the site is stabilized.

assemblies.name: Asphalt paving
assemblies.why: Asphalt weighs about 145 lb per CF in place: tons are area times thickness in feet times 145 over 2,000. Tack coat about 0.05 gallon a SY between lifts; aggregate base under it.

assemblies.name: Concrete curb and gutter
assemblies.why: Concrete is the section area times the length (a 6 in curb with a 24 in gutter is about 1.6 SF), forms both faces, joints every 10 ft.

assemblies.name: Concrete curb
assemblies.why: Concrete is the section area times length (a 6 x 18 in curb is 0.75 SF).

assemblies.name: Concrete sidewalk
assemblies.why: Concrete is area times thickness; control joints every 5 ft across a 5 ft walk come to about 0.2 LF a SF.

assemblies.name: Pavement striping
assemblies.why: A 4 in line uses about one gallon of traffic paint per 300 LF.

assemblies.name: Parking stall striping
assemblies.why: Each counted stall shares lines with its neighbor: about one 18 ft line per stall plus one per row.

assemblies.name: Wheel stops
assemblies.why: Each counted wheel stop with the two anchor pins that hold it to the pavement.

assemblies.name: Sod
assemblies.why: Sod by area with 5 percent for cuts; a pallet covers about 450 SF.

assemblies.name: Seeding
assemblies.why: Seed at about 5 lb per 1,000 SF for a new lawn; mulch at about one bale per 1,000 SF.

assemblies.name: Chain link fence
assemblies.why: Fabric and top rail run the length; line posts every 10 ft; end posts two per run; concrete about 0.1 CY a post.

assemblies.name: Wood fence
assemblies.why: Posts every 8 ft, two or three rails per bay, and pickets at their width plus gap.

assemblies.name: Unit pavers
assemblies.why: Pavers by area with 5 percent for cuts (10 percent on curves); bedding sand at 1 in and joint sand.

assemblies.name: Storm drain pipe
assemblies.why: Pipe along the drawn run in 20 ft lengths with bedding at about 0.1 CY a LF for 12 to 18 in pipe.

assemblies.name: Sanitary sewer pipe
assemblies.why: Pipe in 14 ft lengths along the run with bedding about 0.08 CY a LF for 6 to 8 in pipe.

assemblies.name: Water main
assemblies.why: Pipe along the run in 20 ft lengths; thrust blocks at bends are counted separately; tracer wire runs the length.

assemblies.name: Manholes
assemblies.why: Each counted manhole: base, riser sections to the depth (4 ft sections), cone, and frame and cover.

assemblies.name: Catch basins
assemblies.why: Each counted catch basin with its frame and grate; structures are set to depth in the field.
